topic: A short dynamic warm-up before an easy run

slides.title:
5 warm-up
moves before
your run
slides.subtitle: Five to ten minutes, no gear, right where your run starts.

slides.title: Start warm, not cold
slides.body: Easy moving drills raise your heart rate and warm up your muscles. They take your hips, knees and ankles through the motions of running, so the first mile feels *smoother* and you ease into your pace.

items.title: Leg swings
items.text: 10 per leg, front to back, holding a fence.

items.title: Walking lunges
items.text: 10 slow steps, chest tall, back knee low.

items.title: Butt kicks
items.text: 20 seconds, heels up toward your glutes.

items.title: Ankle hops
items.text: 20 small, springy hops on the balls of your feet.

slides.label: minutes before an easy run
slides.note: A common rule of thumb. Before intervals or a race, warm up a little longer.

slides.title: Long stretches come after
slides.body: Held stretches fit best after your run, when you are warm. Before it, keep moving: dynamic drills get you ready, while long holds can briefly take some spring out of your legs.

slides.quote: Nobody posts the warm-up. It’s still the ten minutes that make the first mile feel like running, not surviving.
slides.author: Northside Run Club

slides.title: Lace up, then loosen up
slides.caption: No track needed. A quiet sidewalk or a park path works just as well.

slides.title: See you at the start line
slides.text: Save this so the playbook is on your phone before your next run.

caption:
Five moves, ten minutes, an easier first mile.

This is our warm-up before every club run: leg swings, walking lunges, high knees, butt kicks and ankle hops. The long stretches wait until after.

Save this for your next run.
